title: Generic inverse partial maps restrict to inverse morphisms
statement: Let $X,Y$ be integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme], with function fields $K(X),K(Y)$ [def-sc-function-field]. Let $f:U_f\to Y$ and $g:U_g\to X$ be morphisms on dense open subsets of $X,Y$, respectively. Let $e:\operatorname{Spec}K(X)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}K(Y)$ be an isomorphism. Suppose the generic restriction of $f$ equals $j_Y\circ e$ and that of $g$ equals $j_X\circ e^{-1}$, where $j_X,j_Y$ are the canonical generic-stalk spectrum maps. There are dense opens $U\subseteq U_f$ and $V\subseteq Y$ and mutually inverse morphisms $f\prime:U\to V$, $g\prime:V\to U$, with $f\prime$ followed by the inclusion into $Y$ equal to the restriction of $f$ to $U$.

proof.text: The generic equations imply dominance: the closed point of the spectrum of the function field maps to the generic point of the target; its closure is the whole target. This is proved by dominant_of_generic_iso.

Factor the generic map of f.comp g through the open domain of g, using its open inclusion monomorphism. Its factor equals e.hom followed by the generic-stalk map into the domain of g. Composing with g gives e.hom followed by e.inv followed by j_X, hence j_X. Repeat with roles reversed. Mathlib PartialMap.equiv_of_fromSpecStalkOfMem_eq identifies each composite with the identity as a partial map. All these calculations are proved in comp_fromFunctionField_of_generic_inverse and the main proof.
Apply the inverse restriction theorem to the two dominant partial maps and the proved equivalences of composites to the identities.

proof_origin.note: Explicit inverse-map restriction argument adapted from the cited proofs; implemented in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_inverse_restrictions_of_generic_inverse
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y]
    (f : X.PartialMap Y) (g : Y.PartialMap X)
    (e : Spec X.functionField ≅ Spec Y.functionField)
    (hf : f.fromFunctionField = e.hom ≫ Y.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint Y))
    (hg : g.fromFunctionField = e.inv ≫ X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X)) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : Dense (U : Set X)) (hUf : U ≤ f.domain)
      (V : Y.Opens) (_ : Dense (V : Set Y))
      (f' : U.toScheme ⟶ V.toScheme) (g' : V.toScheme ⟶ U.toScheme),
      f' ≫ g' = 𝟙 _ ∧ g' ≫ f' = 𝟙 _ ∧
        f' ≫ V.ι = X.homOfLE hUf ≫ f.hom
